name: cpu_slam_ba
title: SLAM bundle adjustment
short_description: Sparse bundle adjustment of a visual SLAM map across all cores.

structured_text.description: Optimises the camera poses and 3D landmarks of a bundled visual SLAM map with sparse bundle adjustment, the back end step that keeps robot and AR maps consistent. The problem is solved with the Ceres Solver, a widely used nonlinear least squares library, using its sparse Schur complement method on all cores. The map, robust loss and stopping criteria are fixed.
structured_text.metric_explanation: The score is the number of complete bundle adjustment solves per minute.
structured_text.value_interpretation: Higher is better. Faster solves let a robot correct drift and close loops more often, and let mapping and photogrammetry jobs finish sooner.
structured_text.reasoning: Bundle adjustment combines many small dense Jacobian evaluations with large sparse linear algebra, a pattern that stresses floating point throughput, caches and memory bandwidth together, much like real SLAM and structure from motion software.
